title: Blade Runner 2099 Reviews Divide Critics Over Its Bleak Tone
excerpt:
Critics disagree on the series' oppressive atmosphere and visual style.
All eight episodes arrive on Prime Video on November 25, 2026.
body_md:
Early reviews of Blade Runner 2099 have highlighted a divide over the science-fiction series' atmosphere. While its visual design has attracted attention, the intensity of its bleakness has become a significant point of disagreement.

Set fifty years after Blade Runner 2049, the story depicts a world where replicants have become the ruling class and humans face oppression. Cora, played by Hunter Schafer, attempts to escape her circumstances by posing as a replicant Blade Runner. She is partnered with Olwen, a dying replicant portrayed by Michelle Yeoh.

The Guardian's Rhik Samadder found the visuals impressive but oppressive, describing the setting as darker than the preceding films. CNET's Aaron Pruner likewise expressed reservations about the bleak atmosphere while acknowledging aspects of the show's execution.

Variety's Alison Herman offered a more enthusiastic assessment, praising Schafer's performance and creator Silka Luisa's approach to the franchise's established world. TVLine's Dave Nemetz was less persuaded by both the relentless bleakness and the visual presentation.

The contrasting responses suggest that noir aesthetics and an uncompromisingly dark narrative will not appeal equally to every viewer. All eight episodes are scheduled to become available on Prime Video on November 25, 2026.
